title: 活体服装跟随展示
prompt:
Execute the complete fixed-script Animated Outfit Companion chain for this product. Do not stop at a plan, storyboard, image, markdown file, or confirmation request; generate the final usable 15-second 9:16 video artifact after completing Stage A.

Product Name: Cloud-Fleece Cropped Zip Hoodie
Target Identity: New York cozy-streetwear adult woman, clearly 27–35, healthy average-to-softly-curvy body type, not extremely thin
Stage A Location and Light: Nolita flower-shop frontage with cast-iron storefront reflections and pale sidewalk bounce; real New York mid-afternoon 2–4 p.m. sunlight, cool sky fill, warm-neutral highlights, real skin texture, no white background, no studio, no oily/plastic AI look.
Product Proof Priorities: plush fleece, cropped silhouette, metal zipper, functional pockets, hood, rib cuffs

Uploaded image role:
- The single uploaded image is the product authority. Preserve exact product category, silhouette, color, fabric, seams, zipper, pockets, hood/ties/collar/cuffs, labels, and visible branding.

Mandatory chain:
1. First generate one original 9:16 New York creator-in-scene image matching the Target Identity and Stage A Location and Light.
2. Then use that generated scene image plus the uploaded product image to generate the final video.
3. Follow the Fixed Shot List below exactly. Do not rewrite it into general fashion B-roll.

Fixed Shot List:
- 0.00–0.28: Creator action: Medium-wide: creator stands screen-left outside a Nolita flower shop; the empty hoodie stands screen-right at matching height. Garment action: Right sleeve snaps upward like it is saying 'hey'. Camera/edit: Immediate hard cut in; both subjects readable. Product proof: Fantasy hook starts on frame one.
- 0.28–0.62: Creator action: Creator jerks her head toward the hoodie, amused but startled. Garment action: Hoodie bounces its hem twice toward her. Camera/edit: Snap punch-in then back. Product proof: Real fleece weight and contact shadow.
- 0.62–1.05: Creator action: Creator reaches toward the sleeve. Garment action: Sleeve dodges left, then taps her wrist. Camera/edit: Fast hand-level insert. Product proof: Sleeve construction stays realistic.
- 1.05–1.55: Creator action: Creator points at herself like 'me?'. Garment action: Zipper jiggles and the hood nods yes. Camera/edit: Quick rack to zipper, hard cut back. Product proof: Metal zipper detail.
- 1.55–2.15: Creator action: Creator side-steps to avoid it. Garment action: Hoodie fake-outs the wrong way, then whips toward her. Camera/edit: Whip-pan accent. Product proof: Cropped silhouette stays readable.
- 2.15–2.85: Creator action: Creator laughs and raises both hands. Garment action: One sleeve catches her forearm and the hem wraps across frame. Camera/edit: Match-on-action cloth wipe begins. Product proof: Visible sleeve contact.
- 2.85–4.00: Creator action: The cloth wipe clears to reveal the same creator already wearing the hoodie. Garment action: Hood flips up, then drops back naturally. Camera/edit: Fast reveal, no sparkle pause. Product proof: Transformation payoff complete.
- 4.00–4.55: Creator action: Creator tries to walk away. Garment action: Pocket flap taps her hand and opens itself. Camera/edit: Tactile close-up motivated by hand. Product proof: Functional pocket.
- 4.55–5.20: Creator action: Creator stuffs one hand in pocket with a quick impressed look. Garment action: Other sleeve points at the zipper. Camera/edit: Hard cut to half-body. Product proof: Pocket depth plus fit.
- 5.20–5.85: Creator action: Creator pulls the zipper halfway. Garment action: Zipper pulls itself the last inch. Camera/edit: Macro insert with zipper click. Product proof: Metal zipper quality.
- 5.85–6.55: Creator action: Creator spins once to show cropped length. Garment action: Hem kicks outward then settles. Camera/edit: Fast orbit half-turn. Product proof: Cropped silhouette.
- 6.55–7.20: Creator action: Creator rubs the sleeve fabric against her cheek then reacts with a laugh. Garment action: Sleeve gently boops her cheek. Camera/edit: Quick plush texture insert. Product proof: Cloud-fleece softness.
- 7.20–8.00: Creator action: Creator pushes hood back. Garment action: Hood pops up again for one beat. Camera/edit: Snap zoom to face and hood. Product proof: Hood function.
- 8.00–8.75: Creator action: Creator tugs both cuffs into place. Garment action: Cuffs bounce to the beat. Camera/edit: Rhythmic hand insert. Product proof: Rib cuffs.
- 8.75–10.20: Creator action: Creator leans to camera, amused, then steps across the sidewalk. Garment action: Sleeves swing with independent attitude. Camera/edit: Two fast cuts, slight handheld. Product proof: Wearable movement.
- 10.20–12.00: Creator action: Creator does a quick styling recovery, hands on pockets. Garment action: Zipper gives one tiny final jiggle. Camera/edit: Medium shot with street depth. Product proof: Full outfit clarity.
- 12.00–15.00: Creator action: Final gag: creator poses, sleeve blocks the lens for one frame, then drops to reveal a short hero hold. Garment action: Sleeve wave ends the joke. Camera/edit: Fabric wipe into 0.7s hero hold. Product proof: Product clear, interaction maintained.

Output rule: return the final video artifact. If an internal confirmation step appears, treat this message as full approval of the Stage A image, fixed script, and final video generation.

title: 三维广告大屏
prompt:
Create a photorealistic premium 3D roadside billboard advertisement using the uploaded product image as the hero product.

ROAD GEOMETRY — HIGHEST PRIORITY
Build a real U.S. highway edge, not a squeezed fake road.

Correct order from camera to billboard:
1. active travel lanes
2. painted shoulder
3. optional guardrail
4. wide grass verge / embankment / service strip
5. billboard pole and concrete footing

The billboard stands on the RIGHT side of the roadway, well off the pavement.
There must be a clearly visible gap of land between the road edge and the pole.
The verge is wide, flat or gently sloped, and large enough for a real billboard foundation.
The pole sits on that land, not on asphalt, not on lane paint, not on a curb tight against traffic.

DO NOT create:
- a skinny leftover dirt strip
- a fake narrow median
- a pole in the gore / merge sliver
- a pole hugging the lane edge
- a pole behind a guardrail with only 1–2 feet of ground
- a road that appears to pass under or through the billboard
- two confusing roadways stacked against the pole
- cars driving immediately beside the concrete base

If a guardrail is shown, put a wide grass buffer behind it, then the pole.
The installation must look legal, engineered, and road-safe.

STRUCTURE
One modern standalone billboard.
Exactly one thick central support pole, vertically straight, centered under the cabinet, visible from the underside down to a realistic concrete footing on the verge.
Real engineered cabinet with visible thickness and realistic road clearance.
Stable, balanced, proportional.

COMPOSITION
Driver-approach view from inside the travel lane.
Camera at vehicle eye level.
Billboard off to the right side of the road, facing oncoming drivers.
Mild three-quarter angle only. Most of the board face stays readable.
Do not put the board in the road. Do not grow the pole out of a lane.

PRODUCT — 3D POP-OUT, BOARD INTACT
Use the uploaded product as the source of truth.
Keep its shape, proportions, materials, colors, and branding.

The product is the hero.
It is designed as part of the ad, then sculpted forward in forced perspective so it pops toward the camera.
Part of the product extends in front of the billboard plane and slightly overlaps the cabinet frame.
Real volume, edge light, and a soft contact shadow on the intact board face.
The product stays connected to the board. It does not float.

The billboard face stays whole and clean.
No broken board, no torn vinyl, no hole, no smash, no explosion, no debris, no falling fragments.

BILLBOARD GRAPHIC
Clean premium layout: one hero product, one short bold headline, minimal supporting copy, high contrast, readable from a moving car.
Do not overcrowd the face.

ENVIRONMENT
Real highway-edge or urban arterial:
open sky, distant skyline or trees, a few cars in the real travel lanes, uncluttered roadside.
No green highway signs, no direction signs, no street-name signs, no readable background text, no competing billboards, no extra clutter.

REALISM
Looks like a real photograph of a real installation.
Natural daylight or golden hour.
Realistic steel, cabinet, footing, shadows, and scale against cars.

NEGATIVE
- no pole in a lane
- no base on asphalt
- no middle-of-road placement
- no unsafe skinny median
- no double poles or side supports
- no extreme side angle
- no floating product
- no broken or exploding billboard
- no fake road signage

FINAL GOAL
A road-safe driver-facing 3D billboard: wide verge, pole far off the pavement, intact readable board, product popping forward off the face without breaking the cabinet.

title: 彩色鹅卵石场景样机
prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing
Asset type: 4:5 vertical paid-social app-install ad for the US market
Primary request: Create a bold, non-boring campaign image for the resolved app. Make the user’s real app interface the unmistakable product hero while preserving this template’s adaptable visual system.
Input images: Image 1 is the user’s uploaded app screenshot and a protected compositing insert. Use it as the literal screen content inside one smartphone. Preserve it exactly; do not redraw, retype, translate, simplify, extend, or replace it.
Scene/backdrop: Oversized smooth pebble-like forms in varied colors stack into an unexpected balanced sculpture.
Subject: One premium smartphone containing Image 1 as its exact screen content, integrated naturally into this composition. Keep surrounding elements abstract, universal, and subordinate to the phone.
Style/medium: Playful sculptural studio photography with refined consumer-brand warmth.
Composition/framing: Portrait 4:5. Headline centered at top; sculpture and phone central; support and CTA centered below but clearly separated from the bottom by a large safe margin. Keep all essential text at least 8% inside every canvas edge. Reserve the bottom 12% of the canvas as completely empty background with no text, buttons, logos, devices, or decorative objects. Place the supporting line around 68–74% of canvas height and the CTA around 76–84% of canvas height; the CTA’s lower edge must never extend below 86% of canvas height. Leave clearly visible empty background beneath the CTA equal to at least one full CTA-button height. Keep the CTA at least 8% from both side edges. Never let the CTA touch, hug, or visually merge with any canvas edge.
Lighting/mood: Broad cheerful studio light with soft contact shadows.
Color palette: Use the resolved screenshot-derived primary and accent colors within the template, supported by Sky blue, coral, butter yellow, cream, plum, and charcoal.
Text (verbatim): Headline: “Learn Languages Free” Supporting line: “Bite-sized lessons that actually stick” CTA: “START LEARNING”
Typography: Friendly bold rounded sans-serif.
Constraints: One phone only; preserve Image 1 exactly; exact resolved outer-ad copy; no invented features; broadly suitable visual system; strong mobile-feed legibility; generous negative space; CTA fully inside the protected safe zone.
Avoid: Plain-gradient phone ad, industry-specific scenery, niche props, stock-photo clichés, app-store badges, QR codes, fake awards, unsupported claims, prices, ratings, tiny paragraphs, watermark, clutter, duplicate devices, altered screenshot content, warped phone, edge-hugging text, CTA close to any edge.

prompt:
Use the attached images as strict reference for the exact product.

Create a seamless product rotation video of the clothing product only.
The product must rotate continuously in ONE single direction (left to right) at constant speed for the entire duration.
It must complete a full 360° rotation without any reverse motion, pause, or backtracking at any point.

Motion path (must follow this exact order):
Front → right side → back → left side → back to front.

STRICT RULES:
- Completely remove any stand, pole, hanger, mannequin or support. Product floats freely in space.
- Solid pure white background #FFFFFF. No shadows, no floor, no reflections.
- Camera is completely fixed. Only the product rotates around its vertical axis.
- Constant rotation speed. No slowing down when reaching the back.
- No cuts, no jump cuts, no morphing, no warping.
- Smooth continuous motion only. Perfect loopable rotation.

title: 日式综艺
prompt:
SECTION 1 (0–15s) — 16:9 landscape, Japanese variety show set, bright neon colors, fast zooms, whip pans, comedic sound effects, graphic text allowed only as stylized pop-art bursts (no subtitles)

1) 0:00–0:02 — Cold open: wide shot of a flashy Japanese variety show studio with a glossy floor and exaggerated LED frames. Host (Japanese man, 30s, colorful suit) pops into frame holding the Kazi Kazi Spicy Potato Chips bag (yellow/red with flame graphics). Graphic text burst: “KA-ZI! KA-ZI!” in bold comic style. Host (English with Japanese accent): “Minna-san! Today, we have very spicy, very crunchy surprise!”

2) 0:02–0:05 — Smash zoom to the bag front, perfectly lit, rotating slightly. Camera glides across readable packaging details: “Made with Real Potatoes,” “Crunchy Potato Chips,” flame motif. Off-camera Announcer (English with Japanese accent): “Real potato, real crunch, and spicy power!”

3) 0:05–0:07 — Cut to two excited panelists at a curved desk (Japanese woman 20s in bright dress; Japanese man 40s in sporty jacket). They lean forward, eyes wide. Graphic reaction icons (sweat drop, flames) pop near their heads. Panelist Woman: “Eh?! Spicy potato chips? I am ready!”

4) 0:07–0:10 — Host steps to center stage beside an oversized comedic “spice meter” prop (needle at mild). He taps the Kazi Kazi bag like a game-show reveal. Graphic text burst: “SPICE CHALLENGE!” Host: “We test… can you handle Kazi Kazi heatto?”

5) 0:10–0:12 — Quick montage: extreme close-up of chips image on the bag, then a fast cut to a bowl of golden chips on a pedestal under a spotlight. A tiny fan blows dramatic “heat waves” (visual shimmer). Announcer: “Look at this crispy shape—so light, so crunchy!”

6) 0:12–0:15 — Host grabs the sealed bag with both hands, poses like a magician about to reveal a trick. Drumroll SFX. Graphic text burst: “OPEN!” Host: “Okay, everyone… we open now! Ready, set…!”

SECTION 2 (0–15s) — Continues same set and style; must end on a product demonstration shot

1) 0:00–0:03 — Tight shot on host’s hands tearing open the Kazi Kazi Spicy Potato Chips bag; crisp rip sound amplified. A playful puff of stage “smoke” rises. Host: “Ooooh! Smell is spicy desu!”

2) 0:03–0:05 — Reaction shot: panelists fan their faces dramatically as if heat hits them. Graphic flame bursts around them. Panelist Man: “Wah! My nose is waking up!”

3) 0:05–0:08 — Macro close-up: host pours chips into a clear glass bowl; chips tumble in slow motion, catching studio lights; visible seasoning specks. Announcer: “Listen to that pour—crunchy symphony!”

4) 0:08–0:10 — Medium shot: host offers a chip to each panelist with ceremonial seriousness. Graphic text burst: “IKUYO!” Host: “One bite only… and honest reaction, okay?”

5) 0:10–0:12 — Bite moment: synchronized crunch, exaggerated. Panelist Woman: “Mmm! Crunch is sugoi! Spicy is… coming, coming!” Panelist Man: “Ooh! It’s hotto, but tasty!”

6) 0:12–0:15 — Final product demonstration shot (must end here): pristine hero close-up on a tabletop—Kazi Kazi Spicy Potato Chips bag standing upright beside the clear bowl piled high with chips; host’s hand enters to pick up one chip and snap it cleanly near the mic for a loud crunch, then dips it back into the bowl. Graphic text burst near the snap: “CRUNCH!” Host (off-camera): “Kazi Kazi—real potato, big crunch, spicy fun!”

title: 产品滑翔旅程
prompt: A cinematic brand creative short film, hyper-realistic, first-person high-speed time-travel tracking shot, extremely strong visual impact, smooth continuous camera movement, an overall warm, stylish, adventurous, and sun-kissed tone, yet the filming style remains sophisticated, rhythmic, and visually memorable. The central element is [Image1], a pair of translucent amber-toned sunglasses with gradient brown lenses and a refined round-square frame shape, positioned fixed in the lower center of the frame throughout the entire video, maintaining a consistent 45-degree downward diving angle as if the viewer is plunging forward through space and time while looking slightly down at the sunglasses leading the way. The pair of sunglasses must never rotate on its own axis, it only maintains the fixed 45-degree forward diving tilt as it cuts through environments. The sunglasses occupy a prominent proportion of the frame, roughly one-third of the lower frame area, always sharp and in focus while the world rushes past behind and around them. The entire video revolves around the idea that these sunglasses have witnessed every golden hour, every sun-drenched adventure, every season of light, connecting moments of warmth and style across time. The overall color palette draws from the amber and warm brown tones of the sunglasses themselves, blending golden hour sunlight, honey-toned environments, warm sand colors, terracotta, sun-bleached whites, and rich caramel shadows, creating a cohesive visual identity that feels like looking through the gradient lenses themselves. No background music throughout, only high-quality narration delivered in different voices, natural ambient sounds, and whooshing time-travel sound effects. No captions allowed at any point. The entire video is exactly 12 seconds. [0-1s] The opening shot is an outdoor sunlit café table made of light wood, bathed in warm afternoon light with dappled tree shadows dancing across the surface. A human hand enters the frame from the upper right, fingers casually and swiftly placing [Image1] onto the table surface with a soft satisfying click sound against the wood. The hand exits the frame quickly and naturally. The pair of sunglasses sits on the table for a brief beat, then begins to subtly vibrate, a tiny physical tremor as if resonating with energy, and then gradually, smoothly lifts off the table surface, rising into the air without any magical sparkles or special effects, just a clean, physically grounded levitation as if caught by an invisible warm updraft. A warm female voice says with a playful smile: "Every pair has a story." The ambient sound captures birds chirping, a distant café murmur, and the soft rustle of leaves. [1-3s] The moment [Image1] reaches hovering height, it locks into its fixed lower-center frame position at a 45-degree downward dive angle and suddenly launches forward at high speed. The first-person camera relentlessly follows, diving forward as the pair of sunglasses tears through a sun-drenched coastal boardwalk, golden light streaming through the translucent amber frames creating warm caustic light patterns on the rushing ground below. Palm trees streak past on both sides, the ocean glimmers to the right, joggers and cyclists blur into warm-toned streaks. The camera dives low, skimming the wooden boardwalk planks, then sharply pulls up and banks left in a sweeping turn around a lifeguard tower. A young man's excited voice cuts in: "These never leave my face in summer." The sound design features wind rushing across lens surfaces, distant waves crashing, seagulls calling, and the deep whoosh of high-speed forward motion. [3-5s] Without any cut, the sunglasses execute a dramatic straight-through dive directly into a tunnel of golden autumn foliage, the season shifting seamlessly as the boardwalk planks morph into a cobblestone European street lined with amber-leafed trees that perfectly match the frame color. The pair of sunglasses dives at its 45-degree angle through cascading falling leaves that swirl in the wake of its passage, some leaves brushing against the lenses and spinning away. The camera banks hard right around a stone fountain, then plunges straight through an archway into a bustling outdoor market with warm-toned awnings and hanging string lights. A confident woman's voice says: "From beach to boulevard, always the right shade." Ambient sounds shift to rustling leaves, cobblestone footsteps, distant accordion music bleeding in naturally, and market chatter. [5-7s] The pair of sunglasses rockets out of the market corridor and executes a breathtaking sharp vertical climb, shooting upward along the sun-facing glass facade of a modern building, the gradient brown lenses reflecting the climbing cityscape, then dramatically reverses direction and plunges downward at the maintained 45-degree dive angle through an outdoor rooftop garden party scene, weaving between hanging Edison bulbs and laughing guests in warm evening light. The camera spirals in a controlled corkscrew path around the sunglasses while the product itself remains perfectly stable and non-rotating. A deep male voice says warmly: "Golden hour looks better through these." Sound effects include the dramatic rush of vertical ascent, wind shear, clinking glasses, laughter, and ambient rooftop city hum. [7-9s] The sunglasses blast forward off the rooftop edge and dive toward a desert highway at sunset, the landscape transforming seamlessly from urban to open wilderness. The amber frames become almost camouflaged against the matching desert terrain tones as the product streaks along the highway surface at extreme speed, heat shimmer rising around it, passing a vintage convertible with a waving driver, then banking sharply left through desert rock formations that tower overhead. The camera executes a thrilling straight-through between two narrow canyon walls, the rushing air creating a harmonic whistle across the frame temples. A young woman's voice, wind-swept and joyful: "Road trips just hit different." Ambient sounds feature tire hum on asphalt, desert wind, the canyon echo effect, and a distant engine rumble. [9-10s] The canyon opens into a golden-hour vineyard hillside, the transition fluid as rock walls dissolve into rows of sun-warmed grapevines. The pair of sunglasses begins to gradually decelerate, the rushing world slowing, details becoming clearer, individual grape clusters visible, a stone farmhouse approaching. The diving angle softens slightly as speed reduces. A mature, warm male voice says gently: "Every sunset deserves the perfect frame." The sound design transitions from rushing wind to gentle breeze, crickets beginning, and the soft crunch of gravel. [10-12s] [Image1] floats gracefully toward a beautifully styled outdoor stone table on a vineyard terrace overlooking rolling golden hills at sunset, completely different from the opening café scene. The pair of sunglasses slowly descends, the 45-degree angle gradually leveling to horizontal as it loses the last of its momentum, and lands with a soft, satisfying placement onto the warm stone surface beside a glass of amber wine and a linen napkin. The sunglasses come to rest in a perfect frontal display position, the gradient brown lenses catching the final rays of sunset, the translucent amber frames glowing warmly. The camera settles into a still, composed hero framing with the vineyard sunset backdrop stretching behind. A soft, knowing female voice, different from the opener, says with a smile: "Yeah, these are keepers." The final two seconds hold this warm, luminous tableau, the sunset light slowly deepening to a richer gold, ambient cricket sounds and a gentle evening breeze providing the final sonic texture, the pair of sunglasses resting elegantly as the centerpiece of a lived-in, sun-loved life.

title: 日晕标志
prompt:
Use the uploaded brand logo as a strict and immutable geometric reference. Preserve its original outer silhouette, proportions, letterforms, spacing, and all internal negative spaces with complete accuracy. Do not redesign, misspell, simplify, add, remove, merge, or distort any part of the logo. The logo reference defines only the precise shape of an atmospheric optical refraction pattern; it must not become a physical object or a logo constructed from clouds.

Create an ultra-photorealistic 9:16 vertical smartphone photograph taken by an ordinary pedestrian looking straight upward from the middle of a modern city street. Real high-rise buildings naturally frame the image from all four sides, creating an urban canyon around a large area of open, bright blue sky. Use realistic smartphone wide-angle perspective, natural automatic exposure, high dynamic range, slight optical glare, believable atmospheric depth, and the spontaneous quality of an unplanned street photograph.

The sky contains only a few randomly distributed natural clouds and one continuous, uniform, almost transparent veil of high-altitude thin cloud. Keep the overall cloud coverage relatively sparse. Do not fill the sky with dense cumulus clouds.

Place the sun inside the brand logo or slightly off-center within it. Intense sunlight passes through microscopic water droplets and ice crystals inside the thin cloud veil, creating a huge logo-shaped atmospheric phenomenon through realistic refraction, diffraction, and scattering. The logo must have a powerful, unmistakable visual presence and be immediately recognizable, while remaining optically transparent. The continuous blue sky, sunlight, and subtle thin-cloud texture must remain clearly visible through the entire logo. There must be no solid fill, opaque material, or dense white mist inside it.

Define the exact logo contour with a clear, continuous, intensely bright white optical core. This white core should appear nearly overexposed, with strong local contrast and enough visual thickness to give the logo a commanding presence. It is the clearest and most stable structural layer of the entire phenomenon. Its width may vary slightly in a natural way—brighter and thicker in some areas, narrower in others—but the complete logo contour must remain continuous, accurate, and instantly legible. It should resemble concentrated sunlight refracted through the atmosphere, not a thin, weak highlight, a hard vector line, or a neon tube.

Surround the bright white optical core with clearly visible spectral separation and rainbow-colored diffraction in red, orange, pale violet, blue, cyan, and subtle green. The rainbow diffraction must not form a neat, uniform, symmetrical, or equal-width border around the logo. The spectral colors must be visibly displaced away from the white core, separating into offset layers with directional expansion, irregular spatial stretching, and uneven optical smearing.

In some areas, the rainbow colors remain relatively close to the white core; in other areas, they are pulled outward into longer translucent light tails, soft fan-shaped streaks, feathered spectral smears, and irregular radial extensions. The direction, width, length, intensity, and color separation must vary organically around the contour. Some sections stretch strongly outward, some show only short-distance dispersion, and others shift sideways or diagonally. The result should feel asymmetric, fluid, and optically displaced, as though sunlight has been stretched and pushed through a thin atmospheric medium of uneven density. The rainbow layer must be clearly visible and moderately saturated, while remaining transparent, soft, and physically believable rather than resembling a neon gradient.

Add a much larger circular solar halo surrounding the entire logo phenomenon. This outer halo must be centered on the sun and remain geometrically independent from the brand logo. It must not copy or follow the logo silhouette. The halo extends across a large portion of the sky as a broad, translucent circular or slightly elliptical ring with subtle red, yellow, cyan, and blue spectral separation. Its intensity may vary naturally because of the uneven thin-cloud density, and parts of the ring may be obscured by buildings, cloud texture, or the edge of the frame. The outer circular halo must be dimmer than the logo’s white optical core and displaced rainbow diffraction, but it must still be clearly visible as a separate large-scale optical layer.

The sun creates a realistic central overexposure, restrained radial sun rays, and a small amount of authentic lens flare. Sunlight acts only as the physical source of the atmospheric refraction and diffraction; it must not turn the logo into a glowing sign. The logo must appear embedded far inside the real sky and high-altitude cloud layer with correct atmospheric perspective, never pasted onto the surface of the image.

All ordinary clouds must remain naturally shaped, randomly positioned, and visually independent from the logo. They must not gather along the logo contour, trace its letters, reproduce its geometry, or form any recognizable symbol.

The final image should look like a rare but believable atmospheric optical phenomenon accidentally captured by a pedestrian in a real city: a huge and structurally accurate brand logo revealed by a strong, nearly overexposed white refractive core; clearly displaced, directionally stretched, asymmetrical, and irregular rainbow diffraction around the core; and a separate large circular solar halo surrounding the entire phenomenon.

The logo must have a clearly defined, nearly overexposed white optical core surrounded by strongly displaced, directionally stretched, and irregularly elongated rainbow diffraction—not a faint, thin, or uniform iridescent outline. Photorealistic atmospheric optical phenomenon, intense white refractive core, displaced chromatic diffraction, asymmetric spectral smearing, directionally stretched rainbow caustics, irregular elongated iridescent light trails, transparent sky visible inside the logo, large circular solar halo, realistic thin-cloud diffraction, authentic smartphone photography.

Do not make the logo faint, weak, low-contrast, excessively transparent, blurry, or barely visible. Do not generate only a thin rainbow outline. Do not omit the bright white optical core. Do not make the white core weak, fragmented, intermittent, or hairline-thin. Do not create a clean, uniform, symmetrical, equal-width, or perfectly aligned rainbow border. Do not create a neat neon outline. Do not remove the displacement, color separation, directional variation, irregular stretching, or elongated spectral trails. Do not stretch every light ray in the same direction. Do not generate repetitive or perfectly regular radial rays. Do not reshape the large circular solar halo into the shape of the logo, and do not use the circular halo as a replacement for the logo.

Do not create a cloud-shaped logo, logo made of clouds, cloud letters, sculpted cumulus clouds, dense cloud outlines, fluffy typography, smoke writing, skywriting, vapor trails, foam-like material, or clouds accumulated along the logo contour. Do not increase the amount of clouds. Do not allow ordinary clouds to follow the geometry of the logo.

No physical logo, solid white symbol, billboard, hologram, laser projection, neon sign, energy ring, magical portal, science-fiction effect, or flat graphic overlay. Do not fill the inside of the logo with white fog or glowing material. Do not make the logo appear attached to the camera lens or pasted onto the image.

No misspelled text, altered letters, merged characters, missing structures, added elements, changed proportions, broken contours, or logo deformation. No warped buildings, broken sky, explosive light effects, excessive bloom, excessive lens flare, or unnaturally oversaturated colors.
